key_insight: No single evaluation rubric can fully measure clinical reasoning in LLMs, so existing tools need to be combined across multiple reasoning dimensions.
clinical_relevance: For safer clinical AI assessment, models should be judged on problem representation, temporal synthesis, differential/management reasoning, uncertainty, and faithfulness—not just exam-style accuracy.
method: Structured narrative review spanning three literatures: medical education assessment tools, clinical LLM benchmarks since 2023, and general long-form generation evaluation.

Mapped six dimensions of clinical reasoning: problem representation, temporal synthesis, differential/management reasoning, counterfactual reasoning, calibrated uncertainty, and reasoning faithfulness.
Proposed combined evaluation design features: binary rubric items, separate completeness vs correctness scores, importance weighting with safety caps, and temporal consistency checks.
evidence_signal: The review found no single instrument covers all six dimensions; evidence is strongest for problem representation and differential/management reasoning, while faithfulness remains weakest with only one identified clinical causal-ablation study.
watch_item: The paper is a design rationale, not a validated instrument, and several proposed evaluations—especially for uncertainty, counterfactual reasoning, and faithfulness over longitudinal free-text records—remain underdeveloped.
paper_title: A rubric landscape for evaluating clinical reasoning in large language models: what exists, what is missing, and what needs to be combined
